name: witr
description: Why is this running? Trace any process, port, container, or file back to what started it - CLI + TUI.
readme_summary: witr is a command-line and TUI tool that traces the origin of any running process, port, container, or file back to its starting point. It helps users understand the causality chain behind system processes, going beyond what traditional tools like `ps` or `lsof` provide by explicitly showing how and why something is running.
key_features: Trace process, port, container, or file origins
Explain the causality chain of how something started
Provide machine-readable JSON output
Offer an interactive TUI dashboard
Support Linux, macOS, Windows, and FreeBSD
Available via multiple package managers (brew, conda, winget, etc.)
Single static binary distribution
primary_use_case: Troubleshooting and understanding the root cause of running processes, services, or resource usage on a system by visualizing their entire startup chain.
cover_image_prompt: A wise old owl, perched on a complex network of glowing roots and branches, peering intently at a single, brightly lit seedling. The roots represent various system layers like containers, services, and shells, all converging to nourish the seedling (a running process). The owl's gaze illuminates the direct causal link from the deepest root to the seedling. Subtle digital particles flow along the roots, hinting at data and system activity. The background is a softly blurred, abstract representation of a computer system. The overall mood is one of insightful discovery and clarity, rendered in a 3D isometric illustration style with a clean, focused composition and a color palette of deep blues, greens, and glowing golden light.

name: simutil
description: It's not just a cross-platform TUI app that quickly opens Android & iOS emulators/simulators
readme_summary: SimUtil is a cross-platform terminal UI application that allows users to quickly launch, manage, and connect to Android emulators and iOS simulators directly from the command line. It provides features like one-key launch, custom launch options, device shutdown, logcat viewing, wireless ADB connection, and extensibility through custom plugins.
key_features: One-Key Launch for emulators/simulators
Android launch options (Normal, Cold Boot, No Audio)
Shutdown devices
Logcat viewer with filtering
Wireless ADB connection (IP, 6-digit code, QR code pairing)
Custom plugin system for external tools (scrcpy, Maestro)
Edit configuration file
Xcode Derived Data cleanup (macOS)
primary_use_case: Streamlining the process of launching and managing Android emulators and iOS simulators from a terminal interface, enhancing developer workflow efficiency.
cover_image_prompt: A skilled conductor standing at a podium in a minimalist, futuristic concert hall, orchestrating a symphony of glowing digital devices. Instead of musical instruments, the conductor gestures towards a large, central screen displaying a clean UI with icons for Android emulators and iOS simulators. With each precise movement, different devices light up and spring to life on the screen, represented by small, vibrant 3D models. Subtle streams of data flow from the conductor's hands to the devices, symbolizing control and launch commands. The overall mood is one of effortless command and organized efficiency, with a clean, modern aesthetic. The repository name 'SimUtil' is subtly integrated into the podium design. Style: 3D isometric illustration with a focus on clear iconography and a cool, tech-inspired color palette.

name: npxskillui
readme_summary: SkillUI is a command-line interface tool that analyzes websites, local codebases, or Git repositories to extract their complete design systems. It packages this information into a format that AI models like Claude can directly use to generate UI code, enabling rapid UI development based on existing design languages.
key_features: Extracts design systems (colors, typography, spacing, components, animations, screenshots) from URLs, local directories, or Git repos.
Supports default static analysis and 'ultra mode' for full visual extraction using Playwright.
Generates `CLAUDE.md` and `SKILL.md` files for AI integration.
Packages extracted design system into a `.skill` ZIP file.
Requires Node.js 18+ and optionally Playwright for ultra mode.
primary_use_case: To reverse-engineer existing design systems from any source (web, local, repo) and make them readily usable by AI code generation tools like Claude for rapid UI development.
cover_image_prompt: A skilled artisan, represented by a digital loom, weaving threads of color, typography, and spacing extracted from a glowing, abstract representation of a website. The loom's output is a perfectly formed UI component blueprint. Subtle code snippets and data particles float around the scene, indicating the technical nature. The background is a clean, modern workshop with soft, ambient lighting. The overall style is a 3D isometric illustration with a focus on clarity and a vibrant, harmonious color palette, subtly incorporating the 'SkillUI' name into the loom's design.

name: docspell
description: Assist in organizing your piles of documents, resulting from scanners, e-mails and other sources with miminal effort.
readme_summary: Docspell is a personal document management system designed to help users organize scanned documents, emails, and other files. It leverages machine learning and NLP to automatically suggest tags, correspondents, and extract information like dates, and also provides OCR, full-text search, and a REST API for integration.
key_features: Document organization and management
Machine learning for metadata suggestion (tags, correspondents)
Natural Language Processing (NLP) for information extraction
Optical Character Recognition (OCR)
Full-text search
REST/HTTP API
Web application UI
Email integration
Android app and CLI support
primary_use_case: Organizing and managing personal or small group documents with automated metadata extraction and search capabilities.
cover_image_prompt: A friendly, organized librarian character is sorting a chaotic pile of scattered papers, emails, and digital files into neat, labeled folders. As the librarian touches each item, it transforms into a glowing, organized digital document with clear tags and metadata appearing around it. Subtle digital particles and faint lines of code flow from the librarian's hands to the organized folders. The background is a clean, modern library setting with a hint of a digital interface visible on a nearby screen. The repository name 'Docspell' is subtly integrated into a sign on the librarian's desk. The image should be in a 3D isometric illustration style with a bright, clean color palette and clear, friendly character design.

name: Web-ScreenRec
description: Screen recorder that requires no installation
readme_summary: Web ScreenRec is a lightweight, browser-based screen recording application that requires no installation. It allows users to record their screen, microphone, and desktop audio simultaneously and can convert the recordings to MP4 format using FFmpeg with a single click.
key_features: Cross-platform screen recording without installation
Simultaneous recording of screen, microphone, and desktop audio
One-click conversion to MP4 using FFmpeg
primary_use_case: To provide a simple, accessible, and installation-free way for users to record their screen and audio directly from a web browser.
cover_image_prompt: A friendly, animated web browser window acting as a magical portal. From the portal, streams of light representing screen, microphone, and desktop audio flow into a central, glowing 'record' button. This button then transforms the streams into a neat, compact MP4 video file that emerges from the portal. Subtle digital particles and a small, clean UI overlay on the browser window hint at the software's function. The background is a soft, gradient digital space, emphasizing ease of use and accessibility. The style should be a clean, 3D isometric illustration with vibrant, friendly colors and clear iconography.
